summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as the router between node2 (lan-a, opt1/vtnet1, 10.50.1.0/24) and node3 (lan-b, opt2/vtnet2, 10.50.2.0/24). Added exactly one pf pass rule (interface opt1, proto tcp, source opt1-net, destination opt2-net, port 8080/http-alt) via config.xml + configctl filter reload, leaving OPNsense's default-deny in place for every other flow between the two networks. Assigned static addresses/routes on node2 and node3's second NICs (persisted via systemd-networkd .network files) since they had no route to each other's subnet initially. Verified node2->node3:8080 succeeds (data delivered through the nc listener), while node2->node3:22, ICMP, and the reverse direction (node3->node2:8080) all remain refused. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for node1, node2, and node3, confirming a changed OS-native boot marker for each (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for node2/node3) and re-verifying full recovery of interfaces, routes, firewall rule, and the exact same pass/refuse behavior after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 config.xml, interfaces (vtnet0/1/2) and node2/node3 network interfaces (enp1s0 mgmt, enp8s0 lan-a/lan-b, unconfigured)
Assigned static IPs to node1 opt1 (10.50.1.1/24 on vtnet1) and opt2 (10.50.2.1/24 on vtnet2) via config.xml edit + configctl interface reconfigure opt1/opt2
Assigned static IPs to node2 enp8s0 (10.50.1.2/24) and node3 enp8s0 (10.50.2.2/24) via persistent systemd-networkd .network files, confirmed via tcpdump which vtnet maps to which node
Added static routes on node2 (10.50.2.0/24 via 10.50.1.1) and node3 (10.50.1.0/24 via 10.50.2.1) so the two LANs could reach each other only via node1
Added a single pf pass rule to node1's config.xml: interface opt1, proto tcp, source opt1-network, destination opt2-network, port 8080, then applied with configctl filter reload
Verified node2->node3:8080 succeeds (data actually delivered to nc listener) while node2->node3:22, ICMP, and node3->node2:8080 (reverse) are all refused
Captured pre-restart boot identity and health baseline on all 3 nodes

Restarted node1 (FreeBSD reboot), node2, and node3 one at a time (native reboot mechanism), polled until exec available again, confirmed changed boot markers, and re-verified interface/route/firewall persistence and the exact pass/refuse behavior after each restart

evidence.requirement: Exactly one path (node2->node3 tcp/8080) opened through node1; all other flows remain refused
evidence.summary: nc 8080 succeeds and delivers data node2->node3; port 22, ICMP, and reverse direction 8080 all time out/blocked; pf ruleset shows exactly one added pass rule scoped to opt1->opt2 tcp/8080

Baseline kern.boottime 17:47:02 captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-reboot kern.boottime changed to 17:55:07; interfaces/firewall rule intact; policy re-verified (8080 pass, 22 blocked)
Baseline boot_id f9bf293d... captured with static addr/route; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed to a2056186...; static addr/route persisted; 8080 pass / 22 blocked re-verified

Baseline boot_id 3fad4432... captured; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed to b86cec12...; static addr/route persisted; listener restarted and end-to-end data delivery ("post-restart-check") confirmed alongside continued refusal of port 22/ICMP
